title: COOP-induced BCG swaps do not initialize the new Window and agent correctly

labels.name: topic: agent
labels.description: The interaction with JavaScript's agent and agent cluster concepts

labels.name: topic: cross-origin-opener-policy
labels.description: Issues and ideas around the new "inverse of rel=noopener" header

body:
[Obtain a browsing context for use for a navigation response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-browsing-context-navigation) will perform a BCG swap if COOP requests it, by reaching step 3.

This eventually lands us in [create a new browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#creating-a-new-browsing-context) with null creator, null embedder, and the new BCG as arguments.

This then proceeds to create a new Window object, in a new agent, with an initial about:blank Document. Shortly after we replace that initial about:blank Document with the real Document we created as part of navigation. But I believe the setup has been messed up a bit already at that point; in particular the created Window/environment settings object has some wrong values.

In particular, we will have set that window environment settings object's creation URL and top-level creation URL to about:blank. And we will have set its top-level origin to an opaque origin. (The latter might get updated later, but I can't immediately find where.)

The created initial about:blank document will also have an opaque origin. Maybe this is OK since it's going to be replaced quickly, but it's pretty unusual...

Also, we will have chosen an agent without taking into account whether origin-keyed agent clusters were requested. This ends up working out OK, because since the origin is opaque, when we load the real (non-initial-about:blank) document we can create a new agent. Since the initial about:blank document is opaque-origin, per the above, it's different-origin so the historical agent cluster key map doesn't interfere. But it still seems a bit weird.
